newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Death toll in Russia blast reaches 56.
newsitem.headline: Death toll in Russia blast reaches 56.

text.p: The death toll from the weekend explosion at a military block of flats in Russia's southern Dagestan region rose to 56 on Monday and President Boris Yeltsin declared Tuesday a day of national mourning.
"As of 2100 (1800 GMT) 95 people had been pulled from the rubble. Of these 56 were dead, including 18 children," a spokesman for the Dagestani regional government told Reuters by telephone.
He said there were about 10 people still unaccounted for, adding that rescue work would continue into a third night.
Half of the nine-storey concrete building, housing mostly families of border guards, collapsed like a pack of cards in the blast early on Saturday morning.
The building was not connected to the gas mains and officials say they suspect sabotage.
News agencies, citing regional officials, said an earlier report that security services had detained a suspect in the explosion was untrue.
Tass news agency quoted official sources as saying the blast might have been gangland revenge for a regional crackdown on arms and caviar smuggling.
Border guards issued a statement describing the explosion as a "terrorist act" by cross-border criminals.
"Those who thus intend to intimidate the border defenders are deeply mistaken," said the statement, adding that the losses had strengthened the guards' resolve to deal harshly with the criminals.

Gangland violence has become commonplace in post-communist Russia. Recently 14 people died in a bomb blast at a Moscow cemetery apparently triggered by a feud between warring factions of an Afghan war veterans' charity with big business links.

On Tuesday flags will fly at half mast across the sprawling Russian Federation and the mass media have been asked not to broadcast light entertainment programmes as a mark of respect for those killed in Saturday's blast.

Dagestan borders Chechnya and some officials have speculated about a link between the explosion and the breakaway region, where an uneasy peace is holding after a 21-month bloody conflict between Russian forces and separatists.
But Chechen rebel leader Zelimkhan Yandarbiyev has denied that separatists were involved in the blast, which he said was aimed at wrecking the peace process.
